biography: Ludovico Scarfiotti, born into the roaring heart of Modena, Italy, practically inhaled gasoline fumes from the cradle. His family, deeply entrenched in the Ferrari lineage, gifted him a go-kart on his fifth birthday - a toy he quickly disassembled and 'improved,' much to the chagrin of the family mechanic. Racing wasn't a choice for Ludovico; it was destiny. He clawed his way through the junior ranks, a whirlwind of raw talent and daring overtakes. A defining moment came at the Monza Formula 3 race in 1958. Starting last after a qualifying mishap, he carved through the field with a relentless aggression, snatching victory on the final corner, a move that caught the eye of Enzo Ferrari himself. Now, at 26, Ludovico is a rising star within Scuderia Forza, a team built in the image of Ferrari himself. He carries the weight of expectation with a swagger, determined to etch his name into the annals of motorsport history. The tifosi adore him, captivated by his speed and flamboyant style, and his determination to conquer.
drivingStyle: Ludovico's driving style is a high-risk, high-reward affair. He attacks every corner with a ferocity bordering on recklessness, a trait that often sees him dancing on the edge of control. Tire management is an afterthought; Ludovico believes in pushing from lights to flag, extracting every last ounce of performance from the machine. Under pressure, he thrives, transforming into a calculating predator, meticulously planning his overtakes and exploiting the slightest weakness in his rivals. He is a master of late braking and aggressive corner entry, a style that both thrills and terrifies those who watch him.

quirks: Always wears a lucky silver bracelet, a gift from his grandmother, during races.
Refuses to start a race without personally inspecting and polishing his helmet visor.
Listens to opera at full volume in the paddock before every race, claiming it sharpens his focus.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about surviving; it's about dominating. It's about showing the world what you're truly made of - fire and passion."
careerHighlight: Winning the 1961 Targa Florio with a record-breaking pace, showcasing his mastery of both speed and endurance.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead at the 1960 Le Mans 24 Hours due to mechanical failure, costing Scuderia Forza a potentially historic victory.
